messages:
Alex (Sales): Quick heads-up — FinReg (EU bank) wants to run a POC but their security team insists on EU-only data residency. They asked for: list of sub-processors, how we enforce regional routing, and a pricing ballpark for Dedicated vs Private. Any blockers?

Maria (Solutions Eng): Short answer: we can do an EU-only POC. Options: Hosted API scoped to EU region with strict routing policy, Dedicated (reserved EU capacity), or full Private (VPC / on-prem) if they require total isolation. I can draft the POC runbook.

Sree (Infra Eng): Routing details — we use request metadata (preferred_region header + tenant tags) to select infra. By default smart-routing prefers region but will fallback to nearest available compatible variant. For strict compliance you can set allow_fallback=false so requests are rejected if EU capacity isn't available.

Sree (Infra Eng): Example routing config we can apply for the POC (we can push this via the console or infra API):

```yaml
routing_policy:
  region_preference: eu-west-1
  allow_fallback: false   # drop or reject non-EU routing for strict residency
  require_subprocessor_approval: true
```

Devon (Security): Important: "EU-only" means not only model execution but also logs, telemetry, metrics export, and backups. Sub-processors typically include cloud provider (e.g., GCP eu-west), metrics/monitoring vendor, error-reporting, SSO provider, and any analytics tooling. We maintain an up-to-date sub-processor register — can share a redacted list for the sales thread. Also confirm BYOK/KMS options for keys and whether they need HSM. :lock:  

Maria (Solutions Eng): For the POC we usually offer two tracks: hosted-EU with EU-only routing + DPA and restricted subprocessors; or Private (VPC) if they want network isolation. Hosted-EU is faster (48–72h). Private takes longer (SOW + infra).

Sam (Support): I'll own the POC ops. Need: customer contact, expected TPS, model choice (Llama2-70B / opt variants), max seq length, and whether they want streaming. Once we have those I can stand up an EU-scoped test namespace. ETA after specs: ~48 hours to get a test endpoint.

Alex (Sales): Pricing ask — can you give a ballpark we can share now? They want to budget before legal review.

Maria (Solutions Eng): Ballpark (very rough): Hosted EU POC — usually free credits + pay-as-you-go; Dedicated EU reserved pool — starts around €6k–€12k/month depending on GPU type and commit. Private on-prem — license + support, one-time setup + monthly support (usually high single-digit k/month). I'll flag exact numbers to finance for a firm quote.

Devon (Security): Also note: if they require sub-processors explicitly signed off, legal will require a DPA/SOW clause and potentially SOC2 + ISO-27001 evidence. I can pull the sub-processor register and the compliance pack (SOC2 report, pen-test summary) to share with them.

Alex (Sales): Can we share the sub-processors and the compliance pack now, or do we need NDAs?

Devon (Security): We can share a redacted subprocessors list and the compliance pack under the standard NDA. If they need full unredacted list/legal wording, Legal will route a formal request. I'll post the redacted link here.

compliance-bot: Compliance pack (redacted subprocessors + SOC2 summary) uploaded: https://internal.redwood.ai/compliance/eu-poc-pack (internal link)

Maria (Solutions Eng): For routing policies, also call out model variants: we can pin to EU-hosted model weights (some open models are mirrored in EU infra). If customer requires model to be on-prem we can do Private.

Sam (Support): Action items:
- @Alex (Sales): confirm contact + expected throughput + model choice
- @Devon (Security): drop redacted subprocessors + compliance pack link (done)
- @Maria (Solutions Eng): prepare POC runbook + config template for allow_fallback=false
- @Sree (Infra Eng): prepare infra ticket for EU test namespace (48h after specs)

Alex (Sales): Will get back today with contact + rough TPS. Also FYI they asked if we can document the routing behavior in the SOW (explicit no-fallback clause). Is that straightforward?

Devon (Security): Yes — we can add a no-fallback clause to the SOW and DPA. Legal will need the exact wording (I can draft).

Maria (Solutions Eng): I'll build the SOW snippet and attach to the POC runbook.

Alex (Sales): Perfect. Thanks everyone — I'll loop the customer in once I have TPS + contact. :thumbsup:

Sam (Support): I'll stand by to kick off infra once you share the specs.

Sree (Infra Eng): One note — if the customer expects extremely heavy KV cache sizes / long contexts we should validate memory footprint for EU pool GPUs before committing. I'll include capacity notes in the infra ticket.

Alex (Sales): Noted. Sending contact now.

(End of thread)
